brief.userPrompt: Wednesday 14 April 2027. The National Weather Service Boulder office has a Red Flag Warning from 08:00 to 20:00 for the foothills: west winds sustained 30 mph with gusts to 58 mph, relative humidity 9 percent. The exercise starts at 05:00 in the SCOEM EOC (Emergency Manager Elena Marchetti, PIO Maya Lindqvist, Sheriff Thomas Briggs, Undersheriff Raymond Cho) with Foothills Electric Cooperative (Operations Director Rosalind Ames, Public Safety Partner Manager Daniel Okoye) having sent its 72-hour and 24-hour partner notices and 48-hour and 12-hour customer notices for Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12; at 06:00 the co-op decides whether to de-energize ahead of 45 mph gusts at 09:00, affecting 3,100 customers including 71 medical baseline households and the Pine Gulch Water District's Well 2; the 312 medical baseline customers must be reached or visited and the notice windows met. At 13:20 a fire is reported near Coyote Draw on County Road 68; by 14:30 it is 420 acres, spotting a mile ahead, and by 17:00 about 2,300 acres moving east-southeast toward Gulch Village (zone PG-03, clearance 55 minutes) and Kestrel Springs. Pressure points: set zone statuses (Warning, Order, Shelter in Place) against projected arrival and clearance times, with the latest order time for each zone; Stonebridge Assisted Living (zone KS-04, 40 residents, 120 minutes, one route on Kestrel Springs Road) must start before an order; Pine Gulch Elementary (140 students, PG-03); contraflow on Highway 305 takes 25 minutes to set up and the Mill Creek Bridge is reported blocked; hydrants in Kestrel Springs rely on a pump station with 8 hours of generator; two foothill cell towers on batteries go dark; a circuit is re-energized by mistake in a zone under an Evacuation Warning, and the co-op and county must agree not to re-energize until the county clears the zone; air tankers and a strike team are requested through the interagency dispatch center; smoke pushes the AQI above 150 in Pine Gulch by 16:00 and the school district and Pine Gulch Medical Center act; Pine Gulch High School opens as a shelter and Mountain View Fairgrounds takes large animals; a post claims Kestrel Springs is burning; the Sheriff and the fire agency must use the same zone statuses and acreage. Decisions the exercise should record: evacuation warnings and orders with clearance time and basis, shelter in place, road control, shelter openings, resource requests, the co-op's de-energize and re-energize decisions, the shutoff notices and medical baseline contacts, the school and facility air quality action. The SimCell plays the National Weather Service, the interagency dispatch center and incident commander, the state fire agency, CDOT, the Red Cross, the care center, the water district, cell carriers, reporters and residents.
constraints: Every county email address uses the exercise domain sawmillcountyco.example; the cooperative uses foothillselectric.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Evacuation products use the zone statuses Evacuation Warning, Evacuation Order and Shelter in Place and the zone names in the plan; fire incident summaries follow the ICS 209 style with acreage and containment from the incident commander; WEAs are 360 characters or fewer; shutoff notices state the circuits, the start, the expected duration and the resource center; times are Mountain Daylight Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the National Weather Service, the interagency dispatch center, the state fire agency, CDOT, the Red Cross, the care center, the water district, carriers, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Ordering evacuations early enough, measured against projected fire arrival and zone clearance time. Keeping power shutoff decisions and evacuation decisions tied together. Giving the public one consistent message, so the Sheriff, the fire agency, the co-op, schools and the hospital all use the same zone statuses and acreage.
overview.threat: On Wednesday 14 April 2027, the National Weather Service Boulder office has a Red Flag Warning in effect for the Sawmill County foothills from 08:00 to 20:00 MDT. The forecast calls for west winds of 30 mph with gusts to 58 mph and relative humidity of 9 percent. Before STARTEX, Foothills Electric Cooperative sent its 72-hour and 24-hour partner notices and its 48-hour and 12-hour customer notices for Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12. At 06:00 the co-op must decide whether to de-energize those circuits ahead of 45 mph gusts expected at 09:00. The shutoff would cut power to 3,100 customers, including 71 medical baseline households and the Pine Gulch Water District's Well 2. At 13:20 a wildfire is reported near Coyote Draw on County Road 68. By 14:30 it covers 420 acres and is spotting a mile ahead. By 17:00 it covers about 2,300 acres and is moving east-southeast toward Gulch Village (zone PG-03) and Kestrel Springs. It threatens the foothills road network, the Kestrel Springs water supply for firefighting, cell coverage and air quality in Pine Gulch. The narrative runs from 05:00 into the evening, with time jumps fitting it into 4 hours of exercise play.
overview.operationalImpact: From early morning, 3,100 co-op customers on Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 are told they may lose power for 24 to 48 hours. Medical baseline customers who rely on powered medical devices are the most urgent: 71 of them are on the affected circuits, and the co-op must reach or visit all 312 on its list. Each call that goes unanswered needs 3 retries and, for the 40 most critical customers, a door visit. Customers are calling the co-op's customer care agents about Well 2 and the Pine Gulch Fire Station community room, which serves as the Community Resource Center. After the 13:20 fire report, dispatchers at the Sawmill County Regional Communications Center must get the status of the nearby circuit (dead, or back-fed by customer generators) before crews engage. The EOC must issue each zone status against its latest possible order time. Gulch Village (PG-03, 55-minute clearance) includes Pine Gulch Elementary with 140 students, so families and buses are on the road. Stonebridge Assisted Living (KS-04) has 40 residents, a 120-minute clearance and one route out on Kestrel Springs Road, so it must start moving before any order. Deputies running zone sweeps and staffing traffic control points report that the Mill Creek Bridge is blocked, while contraflow on Highway 305 needs 25 minutes to set up. In the Highway 305 canyon, sheltering in place may be the safer choice. Engine and crew bosses are on Kestrel Springs hydrants that depend on a pump station with 8 hours of generator fuel. Two foothill cell towers go dark when their batteries run out, which cuts off residents and field units. In a zone under Evacuation Warning, a circuit is re-energized by mistake. By 16:00, smoke pushes the AQI in Pine Gulch above 150, and the school district and Pine Gulch Medical Center must act. Pine Gulch High School opens as a shelter and Mountain View Fairgrounds takes large animals. A social media post falsely claims Kestrel Springs is burning, and reporters are calling for acreage and zone statuses that the Sheriff and fire agency must report the same way.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to set Evacuation Warning, Evacuation Order or Shelter in Place for PG-03, KS-04 and the CR zones by the latest order time (projected fire arrival less zone clearance time, issued 30 minutes earlier where possible, per EOP 4), including moving Stonebridge Assisted Living before any order and deciding on shelter in place in the Highway 305 canyon.

objectives.name: Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to tie the Foothills Electric Cooperative de-energization and re-energization decisions on Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 to evacuation zone status, so that dispatch confirms line status before crews engage, no circuit is restored in a zone under Evacuation Warning, and Well 2, the Kestrel Springs pump station and the 71 medical baseline households are protected.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to put out one set of zone statuses, acreage and road statuses that the Sheriff, the fire agency, the co-op, the school district and Pine Gulch Medical Center all use, through WEAs of 360 characters or fewer, SawmillAlert and media briefings, and to correct the false report that Kestrel Springs is burning.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to apply the EOP 5 EOC decisions and the SENTCS 3 and 5 procedures (sweep reporting every 15 minutes, traffic control points, Highway 305 contraflow with CDOT, the hourly shared road status list, opening shelters at Pine Gulch High School and Mountain View Fairgrounds) when the Mill Creek Bridge is blocked and the foothill cell sites fail.

roles.name: Emergency Manager (EOC Command)
roles.team: Team A: Emergency Manager / EOC Command
roles.description: Manages the county EOC: activation level, zone status records and their basis, shelters, resource requests and state and federal declaration requests.
standingOrders: Clock First: track each zone's latest order time and push the decision 30 minutes before it, not when it arrives.
One Board: no zone status, acreage or road status leaves the EOC until it matches the shared board.
Ask Early: request buses, ambulances, mutual aid and the state's help before local capacity runs out, not after.

roles.name: Sheriff (Evacuation Branch)
roles.team: Team B: Sheriff and Evacuation Branch
roles.description: Owns evacuation orders and warnings, shelter in place decisions, zone sweeps, traffic control points, road control and Highway 305 contraflow through the Undersheriff.
standingOrders: Order Early: a zone must be empty before the fire arrives, so a warning that comes late is a failure even if it is accurate.
Know the Egress: before ordering people onto a road, confirm it is open; where there is no safe road, consider shelter in place.
Same Words: use only the plan's zone names and status terms, and agree acreage and statuses with the Fire Chief before speaking.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns public alerts, media statements, rumor control and the joint messaging with the co-op, the schools and the medical center so that every message names its zones and matches their status.
standingOrders: Truth Over Reassurance: say what is known with its time; never deny a threat to calm callers.
Verify Fast: confirm every rumor with the EOC board before you knock it down, then knock it down within the hour.
One Voice: the co-op, schools and hospital repeat the county's zone statuses; work out any differences in private, not in public.

roles.name: Dispatch Supervisor (Sawmill County Regional Communications Center)
roles.description: Manages the Regional Communications Center: call intake, alert transmission (WEA, SawmillAlert, EAS), the time each zone status is set on the map, unit status and line-status checks with the co-op.
standingOrders: Lines Are Live: until the co-op confirms a circuit is dead and has no generator back-feed, tell units the line is energized.
Stamp the Time: log the time and the authority for every zone status before you send the alert.
Plan for Silence: when cell sites fail, shift field units to radio and tell the EOC which areas cannot receive alerts.

roles.name: Fire Chief (Pine Gulch Fire Protection District)
roles.description: Owns fire strategy and tactics, spread projections and arrival times for each zone, requests for evacuation, resource orders and acreage and containment figures until Unified Command forms.
standingOrders: Field Over Screen: if the map and the crews disagree on where the fire is, trust the crews and update the projection.
Request, Don't Wait: ask the Sheriff for orders as soon as a zone's arrival time minus clearance time comes within reach.
Water Watch: track the pump station's generator fuel and plan for the hydrants going dry before they do.

roles.name: Operations Director (Foothills Electric Cooperative)
roles.team: Team F: Electric Cooperative Operations Director
roles.description: Owns the decision to de-energize and re-energize Circuits 4 to 17, line patrols, customer and partner notices and medical baseline outreach, working with the Public Safety Partner Manager.
standingOrders: Thresholds, Not Pressure: de-energize when the plan's criteria are met (Red Flag Warning, gusts of 45 mph or more, fuel moisture of 8 percent or less, circuit cannot be patrolled) regardless of complaints.
No Restore Without Patrol: no circuit is re-energized until it has been patrolled end to end, gusts have stayed below 35 mph for 2 hours and the EOC has confirmed the zone's status.
Reach, Don't Just Dial: count a medical baseline customer as reached only after a confirmed contact; use retries and door visits.

phases.title: Red Flag Morning
phases.goal: Tests whether the co-op and the EOC act early on an uncertain fire-weather forecast. That means making the shutoff call on Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 against the thresholds in the Foothills Electric Cooperative plan section 3, and protecting medical baseline customers, Well 2 and the critical facilities before any fire starts.
beats: (05:00) An exercise-marked NWS Boulder Red Flag Warning remains in effect for the Sawmill County foothills from 08:00 to 20:00 MDT: west winds of 30 mph, gusts to 58 mph, RH 9 percent. At 05:15, co-op weather stations on Circuits 6 and 11 read gusts of 38 mph (sustained 22 mph), still below the 45 mph trigger. Field staff report fuel moisture of 7 percent. Operations Director Rosalind Ames must decide by 06:00 whether to de-energize ahead of the 45 mph gusts forecast for 09:00. The shutoff would affect 3,100 customers, 71 medical baseline households and Pine Gulch Water District Well 2.

(06:00–07:30) If the co-op de-energizes, the at-shutoff notices go out under co-op plan section 4. These include direct calls to the 14 critical facilities, among them Stonebridge Assisted Living, 911 and the two cell towers. Medical baseline calls show 9 no-answers after 3 retries, and 4 of them are on the list of 40 most critical households that need a door visit. Customer care agents are taking calls about whether Well 2 will keep pumping and whether the Pine Gulch Fire Station community room (the Community Resource Center) opens at 07:00.
(07:15) Noise item: dispatch reports a stalled hay truck on Highway 305 at the canyon mouth that blocks one lane for 40 minutes. It has nothing to do with the fire weather but takes up a deputy.

(05:55) The co-op partner pre-brief call under co-op plan section 5, led by Daniel Okoye with Emergency Manager Elena Marchetti on the line. The co-op gives circuits, weather and the decision, and the county checks the zone map against the circuits that serve PG-03, KS-04 and the CR 68 zones. During the call, Superintendent Dr. Tamara Fuentes asks whether Pine Gulch Elementary (140 students) should hold classes, release early or close on a Red Flag day with no power.

phases.title: Smoke at Coyote Draw
phases.goal: Tests initial size-up and line-status coordination once the fire starts: dispatch confirms the circuit is dead before crews engage. Also tests whether the EOC sets Evacuation Warning under SENTCS 2 early enough and starts Stonebridge moving, while competing reports and media pressure build.
beats: Time jump to 13:20. A 911 caller reports smoke and flames near Coyote Draw on County Road 68. Pine Gulch Fire Protection District units under Chief Dwight Kowalski are dispatched. Before crews engage near the line, the Regional Communications Center (Supervisor Joanne Pettibone) must get the co-op to confirm whether the nearby circuit is dead or back-fed by customer generators.

(13:45) Red herring: a resident calls in a second start on Kestrel Springs Road. A Kestrel Springs Volunteer Fire unit under Chief Marta Oyelaran finds a smoldering legal burn barrel that is already out. If the report is not run down, it gets into partner traffic.

(14:30) Visual for the room: a field photo and a simulated FIRMS hotspot cluster put the fire at 420 acres. It is spotting about a mile ahead toward Gulch Village under west-northwest wind. The IC must decide whether to request that the EOC set PG-03, PG-01 and the CR 68 zones to Evacuation Warning under SENTCS 2. A Warning triggers the SawmillAlert text and voice message, deputy notification of the 214-household registry, and calls to Stonebridge Assisted Living, Pine Gulch Elementary and the two campgrounds.

(14:35) Stonebridge Assisted Living (KS-04, 40 residents, 120-minute clearance, one route out on Kestrel Springs Road) asks the EOC whether to start moving residents now, before any order. At the same moment, a reporter with a 15:00 deadline calls PIO Maya Lindqvist for acreage and zone statuses. The reporter already has a different number from a fire district radio scanner post.

(14:40) Partner asks: the Pine Gulch Water District says the Kestrel Springs pump station feeding the firefighting hydrants is on generator with 8 hours of fuel. It asks for priority refueling and the co-op's restoration plan for that feed.

phases.title: Go Now or Shelter
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's single decision point: the Sheriff and EOC set Evacuation Order or Shelter in Place for PG-03, KS-04, the CR zones and the Highway 305 canyon by the latest order time. They do this while the Mill Creek Bridge is blocked, cell sites fail and a Unified Command forms with the state.
beats: DECISION POINT (15:10): the fire's projected arrival at Gulch Village leaves little margin over PG-03's 55-minute clearance. Deputies under Undersheriff Raymond Cho report the Mill Creek Bridge blocked, and Highway 305 contraflow with CDOT needs 25 minutes to set up. Sheriff Thomas Briggs must choose. One option is an Evacuation Order now, which puts Pine Gulch Elementary's 140 students on buses and families on a single road under smoke. The other is Shelter in Place for the Highway 305 canyon while waiting for contraflow. That leaves residents in the fire's path if the projection is late. Both choices have a real cost in lives at risk.

(15:30) The fire exceeds local district capacity. The Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control takes the lead, and a Unified Command forms with the Sheriff under EOP 3. Mutual aid comes through the interagency dispatch center, and players must state who commands the evacuation branch and the traffic control points. Sweep reports must come in every 15 minutes under SENTCS 5.

(15:45) The two foothill cell towers on the de-energized circuits go dark as their batteries run out. Field units lose phone and data, and registry households in KS-04 and along CR 68 cannot receive the SawmillAlert voice message. Deputies must sweep door to door, and Stonebridge reports that 12 non-ambulatory residents are still waiting for transport.

(16:00) Simulated AirNow data puts the Pine Gulch AQI above 150 (Unhealthy). The school district must decide on reunification versus sheltering students, and Pine Gulch Medical Center must decide on air handling and possible patient moves. Pine Gulch High School opens as a shelter, and Mountain View Fairgrounds stages the volunteer animal evacuation team.

(16:15) A widely shared social media post with an old photo claims Kestrel Springs is burning. The PIO must issue a correcting message within 30 minutes: a WEA of 360 characters or fewer plus a SawmillAlert, naming zones and statuses exactly as they appear on the zone map. The Sheriff, the fire agency, the co-op, the school district and the hospital must all cite the same acreage.

phases.title: Holding the Line
phases.goal: Tests stabilization and recovery: keeping re-energization tied to zone status, keeping critical infrastructure running, notifying outside parties, and planning a phased return to service on the co-op plan section 3 re-energization criteria.
beats: Time jump to 17:00. The IC reports the fire at about 2,300 acres with 0 percent containment, moving east-southeast toward PG-03 and Kestrel Springs, in an ICS 209-style summary. The EOC starts the hourly shared road status list: Mill Creek Bridge, Highway 305 contraflow, Kestrel Springs Road and CR 68. Every partner must use this list in place of their own versions.

(17:40) Hurdle: a co-op crew re-energizes a segment of Circuit 11 that serves a zone under Evacuation Warning. This breaks the co-op plan section 5 rule that the co-op holds re-energization until the county declares the zone safe. Dispatch must warn crews, the co-op must de-energize the segment again, and the EOC must find out how the miss happened.

(18:30) The Kestrel Springs pump station generator falls below 3 hours of fuel. The fuel supplier cannot get through the closed CR 68 traffic control point, so players must arrange an escorted delivery or a backup pump while hydrants are still in use.

(19:00) Outside-party notifications per SCFR 9: the state utilities regulator about the mistaken re-energization and the shutoff, CDPHE about smoke, the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management about the shelter population, and neighboring counties about evacuees.

(20:00) Gusts are easing, but re-energization requires gusts below 35 mph for 2 hours and 4 to 8 hours of daylight patrol. The EOC and co-op agree on a phased restoration starting the next morning: Well 2, the Pine Gulch Medical Center feed and the medical baseline households first. Zones held under Evacuation Warning stay de-energized. Repopulation criteria are set, and then ENDEX.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during play. Go around the room one team at a time (Sheriff, fire, co-op, EOC, PIO, schools and hospital, Red Cross) and write every answer on the whiteboard in two columns before anyone discusses them, so the loudest voice doesn't decide what the lessons are.

questions.text: At I-13 (15:10), Battalion 1 told you the latest order time for PG-03 was now. At the same moment the Mill Creek Bridge was blocked, and CDOT needed 25 minutes to set up Highway 305 contraflow under quarter-mile smoke. At 14:30 (I-09), the chief had already given you a 14:50 EOC push. What stopped you from ordering PG-03 and the CR zones at 14:50? When did you decide between an order and shelter in place for the people who would end up in the 305 canyon, and where was Stonebridge Assisted Living at that point? What one piece of information would have let you decide 20 minutes earlier?

At 05:15 (I-02), the station readings of 38 and 37 mph gusts were still below the co-op's 45 mph / 25 mph trigger, but the models and Dale Ostrowski's field report both pointed past it. Did you de-energize on the forecast or wait for the measured gust, and did the county EOC know your answer before six? Then at I-18b, power came back in PG-01 while the zone was still under warning, and families started driving back from the shelter. Who checked the zone status before that restore? Did dispatch ever confirm line status to crews working in the zones?

By 16:17 (I-16b), the public had three different acreage figures: 1,500 from the school district, 3,000 on the Channel 9 chyron, which cited the co-op outage map, and about 2,300 at the fire line, plus a fake photo saying Kestrel Springs was burning. Who owned the single set of acreage, zone statuses and road statuses, and how fast did it reach the co-op call center, the school district and Pine Gulch Medical Center? How long did it take to put out a correction in a WEA of 360 characters or fewer, and what did the 911 callers asking which way to go hear in the meantime?

At 06:36 (I-03b), Nextdoor was saying Well 2 would shut down at 8 and Gulch Village was being evacuated. At 14:36 (I-10b), Channel 9 had a 15:00 deadline and was asking whether the shutoff started the fire. What did you tell the public and the media before you had confirmed facts? Did your early holding statements about water, the Community Resource Center and the 71 medical baseline households hold up later? What would you say differently to the state representative's office by 18:15?

With the Mill Creek Bridge blocked and the foothill cell sites down, which of the SENTCS 3 and 5 procedures actually ran: sweep reports every 15 minutes, traffic control points, the hourly shared road status list and the shelter openings at Pine Gulch High School and Mountain View Fairgrounds? At what moment did you stop trusting the reports reaching the EOC? How did you decide on the 31 children in the unpowered elementary gym at AQI 174 (I-16)?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: National Weather Service Denver/Boulder forecast office, fire weather desk (forecaster on duty)
simcellScripts.trigger: The EM or the co-op Operations Director calls Boulder after I-01 to ask whether the 45 mph gusts will really arrive by 09:00, or asks for a spot forecast or IDSS briefing once the Coyote Draw Fire starts (I-07 / I-09).
hardQuestions: "I can give you confidence, not certainty. Moderate to high that gusts top 45 by mid-morning, and the timing could slip an hour either way. What decision are you making, and by what time? Tell me that and I'll brief to it."
"You want a spot forecast for Coyote Draw? Send me the request with the fire's latitude and longitude, the elevation, the size and the time you need it. I can't build it from 'near Gulch Road.'"
"Do your co-op stations at Coyote Ridge and Gulch Saddle report to us? If I can't see your observations, I'm forecasting blind on the canyon mouths."
"Who on your end gets my wind-shift update: the Fire Chief, the EOC or both? If I call one number and it doesn't reach the evacuation branch, that's on your side."
concessions: Once the caller names the decision and its deadline, gives a scripted IDSS briefing with gust timing (strongest 9 AM to 4 PM along the foothills and canyon mouths) and the confidence level.

After a properly formatted spot forecast request with location and size, delivers a spot forecast. It keeps west-northwest winds of 28–31 mph gusting near 50 through the afternoon and gives a slow decrease after 20:00, with gusts below 35 mph from about 22:00.
Once the co-op agrees to share its station observations, adds Coyote Ridge and Gulch Saddle to the briefing and offers a callback if a wind shift is forecast.

"If I open a shelter for your people, who's paying, and is that under a mutual aid request or just a phone call? I need it in writing to my EOC."
"Channel 9 says 3,000 acres and Kestrel Springs under evacuation. Your Nextdoor says 1,200. What number do I give my commissioners?"
"Is anything coming my way? Do I need to stand up my own traffic control on the plains side of Highway 305?"
concessions: After receiving the current zone status list with the time it was set, agrees to direct those households to the Pine Gulch High School shelter or to hold them overnight.
After a written mutual aid or shelter request from the Sawmill EOC, opens an overflow site of up to 40 cots, which helps close the 31-cot gap.
Once given a single acreage figure with a time and source from Unified Command, uses only that figure in its own public messages.

"Under a Unified Command with the Sheriff, who runs the Evacuation Branch and the traffic control points, and who signs off on acreage? I need names before my IC trainee walks in at 16:15."

"Is Gulch Village under an order or a warning? What's the difference for my viewers? And which zones, by name? Your neighbors at the school district told callers 1,500 acres."
"Did the power shutoff start this fire? The caller said flames were under the line. If you won't answer, I'll say the county and the co-op declined to comment."
"The power came back on in PG-01 while it was under a warning. The state representative is going on my air at 18:30 to say the shutoff was mishandled. Do you want to respond before she does?"
concessions: Given a single acreage with a time and source and the zone statuses named by zone ID, runs those figures and corrects the 3,000-acre chyron on the next update.
Given a scheduled briefing time and a named spokesperson (the PIO or a Unified Command spokesperson), holds the 'declined to comment' line and promises to air the joint statement.
After a joint county–co-op statement on the PG-01 re-energization that names what happened, when it was de-energized again and the zones affected, airs it next to the representative's comments.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. The aim is to test the plans of the Sawmill County EOC, the Sheriff's Office, the Regional Communications Center, Pine Gulch Fire Protection District and Foothills Electric Cooperative, not to grade the people in the room.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the weather, fire behavior, acreage and timings in each module even where they differ from what they would expect on a real Red Flag day.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including the Sawmill County EOP, SENTCS and the Foothills Electric Cooperative PSPS plan. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and record the gap.
Players know only what the module narratives and the delivered injects tell them. Information that reaches one role has not reached the others unless a player passes it on in the room.
Decisions are made at the speed they would be made in a real event. When a decision depends on a partner outside the room, players ask the SimCell for it rather than assuming the answer.
artificialities: Time jumps forward between modules (to 13:20, 15:00 and 17:00 MDT). Players are told what happened in the gaps rather than playing it out.

The SimCell plays every person and agency outside the room. That includes the National Weather Service Boulder fire weather desk, CDOT Region 4, the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control, Colorado DHSEM, CDPHE, the Colorado PUC, Northern Colorado interagency dispatch, the Pine Gulch Water District, the school district, Pine Gulch Medical Center, Stonebridge Assisted Living, the Red Cross, the cell carrier, the media, elected officials, neighboring counties and residents.

Systems are named as they appear in the plans but are not touched. No real WEA, EAS, SawmillAlert, CAD, breaker or co-op outage-map action is taken. Weather products, FIRMS and AirNow data, and the fire size are all simulated and marked EXERCISE.
Injects arrive on paper or on screen as radio calls, phone calls, emails, posts and status boards. One facilitator may voice several callers.
The exercise clock is compressed. Each module covers several hours of incident time in about one hour of discussion.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: Red Flag Morning (05:00 to about 09:00 MDT, Wednesday 14 April 2027)**

It is 05:00 MDT. The SCOEM EOC in Pine Gulch is at normal status with the morning duty staff: Emergency Manager Elena Marchetti and PIO Maya Lindqvist. Sheriff Thomas Briggs and Undersheriff Raymond Cho are on call. It is still dark and 41°F, with a light west breeze and a clear sky. Relative humidity is already falling through 18 percent. There are no fires in the county.

Foothills Electric Cooperative has sent its 72-hour and 24-hour partner notices and its 48-hour and 12-hour customer notices for Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12. Those circuits serve 3,100 customers, including 71 medical baseline households and Pine Gulch Water District Well 2. Overnight traffic at the Regional Communications Center has been quiet, and every foothill cell site and fire station reports normal. Buses for Pine Gulch Elementary (140 students) roll at 07:15. The co-op's de-energization decision is due at 06:00.
keyIssues: Make the 06:00 de-energization call on Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 when measured gusts are still below the trigger but the forecast is above it
Protect the medical baseline households, Well 2, Stonebridge and the other critical facilities before power drops
Decide when the EOC activates, and at what level, on a Red Flag day with no fire yet
Get ahead of rumors about water, the Community Resource Center and evacuations
Match each circuit to the evacuation zone it serves, and decide what the shutoff means for schools

discussionQuestions.text: Operations: Gusts at the co-op stations are in the high 30s, the forecast calls for 45 to 52 mph by 09:00, fuel sticks read 7 percent, and line patrol cannot reach Circuit 12. **Module 4: Holding the Line (17:00 to 20:00 MDT)**

It is 17:00 MDT. The Incident Commander's summary as of 16:55, under Unified Command with DFPC since 16:15, puts the Coyote Draw Fire at about 2,300 acres with 0 percent containment. It is spreading east-southeast toward Gulch Village (PG-03) and Kestrel Springs, with spotting up to 1 mile ahead. Gulch Saddle reads west-northwest 28 mph, gusting 47 mph, with relative humidity at 8 percent. Strike team ST-CO-4417 is on scene and 2 SEATs are cycling. The Type 1 helicopter is still unable to fill. About 900 structures are threatened.

Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 have been dead for 9 hours. The Pine Gulch High School shelter has 212 registered, and Mountain View Fairgrounds holds 47 horses and 19 head of cattle. Since 16:00 the Fire Chief, the co-op, CDOT and the school district have each sent out their own road lists, and those lists disagree. The EOC is starting a single hourly shared road status list (17:00 issue, for players to confirm): Mill Creek Bridge is Controlled, one lane, responders in and residents out. The Highway 305 canyon is in contraflow, outbound only. Kestrel Springs Road is Controlled at the KS-04 traffic control point. CR 68 is Closed east of Coyote Draw. From this hour on, every partner uses this list instead of its own. From here to ENDEX the story clock runs faster than the exercise clock (about two hours of story in the last hour of play), so the times on the cards are story times.

Get every partner using the one shared road status list
